target: Ни ты, ни я не знаем правду.
english: Neither you nor I know the truth.
tip: ни ... ни (ni ... ni = neither ... nor) still needs не on the verb. не знаем (ne znaem = we do not know) keeps the double negative English drops.

target: Они строили дом два года и наконец построили его.
english: They built a house over two years.
tip: One sentence, two aspects. строили (stroili) shows the building in progress, построили (postroili) marks it finally completed.

target: Почтальон ехал на велосипеде под дождём с полной сумкой.
english: The postman rode his bicycle through the rain with a full bag.
tip: ехал (ekhal = was riding) is the vehicle verb. Russian picks ехать (ekhat) for wheels and идти (idti) for on foot, a split English does not mark.

target: Я ничего не слышал об этом.
english: I haven't heard anything about this.
tip: о (o) becomes об (ob) before a vowel sound: об этом (ob etom = about this), but о книге (o knige = about a book).

english: Good night, sweet dreams!
tip: Russian wishes drop into the genitive: сладких снов (sladkikh snov = sweet dreams) literally means of-sweet-dreams.

english: I am reading an interesting book.
tip: A feminine direct object takes -у/-ю: интересную книгу (interesnuyu knigu = interesting book), changed from книга (kniga).

english: The engineer always plays chess.
tip: Playing a game uses играть (igrat) plus в (v): играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess).

english: Let's drink to your health!
tip: Toasts use за (za) plus the accusative: за ваше здоровье (za vashe zdorovye = to your health).

english: Many tourists come here in summer.
tip: много (mnogo = many) forces the genitive plural: много туристов (mnogo turistov = many tourists).

english: I live in a big city.
tip: Location after в (v) uses the prepositional case: в большом городе (v bolshom gorode = in a big city).

target: Он любит свою жену и детей.
english: He loves his wife and children.
tip: Third person needs свой (svoy) for one's own: свою жену (svoyu zhenu = his own wife); using его (yego) would mean another man's wife.

english: Take care of yourself and get some rest.
tip: себя (sebya = oneself) keeps one form for every subject: береги себя (beregi sebya = take care of yourself).

english: It's half past nine–time to go.
tip: Russian time counts toward the next hour: половина десятого (polovina desyatogo = half of the tenth) means 9:30, not 10:30.

english: We live on the fifth floor.
tip: Floors take на (na), not в (v): на пятом этаже (na pyatom etazhe = on the fifth floor).

target: Эта куртка стоит пять тысяч рублей.
english: This jacket costs five thousand roubles.
tip: From five up, the counted noun goes genitive plural: пять тысяч рублей (pyat tysyach rubley = five thousand roubles).

target: Дождь идёт уже третий день подряд.
english: It has been raining for the third day in a row.
tip: Rain uses the motion verb идёт (idyot = goes): дождь идёт (dozhd idyot = it is raining), literally the rain walks.

target: Закройте дверь за собой, когда будете уходить.
english: Close the door behind you when you leave.
tip: After когда about the future, Russian keeps future tense where English uses present: когда будете уходить (kogda budete ukhodit = when you leave).

target: Зимой мы всегда пьём чай с мёдом.
english: We always drink tea with honey in winter.
tip: Зимой (zimoy = in winter) is instrumental with no preposition; seasons show 'in' by case alone.

target: Город был основан более пятисот лет назад.
english: The city was founded more than five hundred years ago.
tip: Passive past uses был (byl) plus a short participle: был основан (byl osnovan = was founded).

english: Fresh bread smells wonderful.
tip: After sense verbs like пахнет (pakhnet = smells), Russian uses an adverb, not an adjective: пахнет замечательно (pakhnet zamechatelno = smells wonderfully).

english: What a magnificent building!
tip: Exclamations use какой (kakoy = what a), agreeing with the noun. Neuter здание (zdaniye = building) takes the neuter form Какое (Kakoye).

english: I'm cold, close the window.
tip: Feelings put the person in the dative: мне холодно (mne kholodno = I am cold), literally to-me cold. Also тепло (teplo = warm), грустно (grustno = sad).

english: Father liked the new restaurant.
tip: With понравился (ponravilsya = appealed) the thing liked is the subject and the liker goes in the dative: Отцу понравился ресторан (Ottsu ponravilsya restoran = to father appealed the restaurant).

english: Brother needs a new phone.
tip: нужен (nuzhen = needed) agrees with the thing needed, not the person: masculine телефон (telefon = phone) gives Брату нужен телефон (Bratu nuzhen = brother needs).

english: Big cities have many problems.
tip: много (mnogo = many) is followed by the genitive plural: много проблем (mnogo problem = many problems), not the plain plural проблемы (problemy).

english: The last bus leaves at eleven.
tip: Clock times use в plus the accusative number: в одиннадцать (v odinnadtsat = at eleven). No extra word for at is added beyond в.

english: There is a big park on the corner.
tip: на углу (na uglu = on the corner) is a street corner outside; в углу (v uglu) is an inside room corner. Same noun угол (ugol), different preposition.

english: We are talking about an interesting movie.
tip: о (o = about) becomes об before a vowel sound: об интересном фильме (ob interesnom filme = about an interesting movie).

target: Извините, не подскажете, как вас зовут?
english: Excuse me, could you tell me your name?
tip: Names use зовут (zovut = they call), a they-form with no subject: как вас зовут (kak vas zovut), literally how you they-call = what is your name.

target: Без хорошего образования трудно найти работу.
english: Without a good education it's hard to find work.
tip: без (bez = without) takes the genitive: без хорошего образования (bez khoroshego obrazovaniya = without a good education).
